_comment: Lexicon for scripts/construct_classifier.py. It decides, from file and folder NAMES only, whether a time-lapse images mitochondrial fluorescence. All matching is case-insensitive. Edit this file (not the Python) to adapt the filter to another lab's plasmid table or naming habits.
_how_to_adapt: 1. columns: map each logical field to the EXACT header text of your plasmid spreadsheet (exported as CSV). Leading/trailing spaces and case are ignored when matching headers.

2. localization_synonyms: map every value that appears in your localization column to one canonical value. Only the canonical value given in mito_localization counts as mitochondrial. Unlisted values are kept as 'other' (treated as not mitochondrial).

3. direct_mito_keywords: tokens that, when present in a file name, are strong enough to call the file MITO on their own (e.g. your lab writes 'mls' or 'mito' in every mito movie). Each alias may contain '-', '_' or ' ', which match an optional separator in file names.

4. common_markers: mito dyes, reporters and proteins that suggest, but do not prove, mito fluorescence. They never produce MITO automatically; they send the file to REVIEW with high priority so a person checks it.

5. fp_vocabulary: every fluorescent protein spelling your lab uses, with its class (constitutive, photoactivatable, photoconvertible, sensor) and display channel color (green, red, far_red, blue). Longest alias wins.

6. boundary: 'none' = match anywhere (even inside a longer word); 'left' = must not be preceded by a letter; 'both' = must not touch a letter on either side. Digits, '_', '-', spaces and string edges all count as boundaries, because names concatenate dates and IDs (e.g. 05feb2025obf01).

7. id_matching / numeric_id: plasmid IDs are parsed as letter prefix + integer (+ optional '-n' / '_n.n' suffix), so OBF001, obf01 and obf0001 are the same plasmid. Pure numeric IDs (e.g. Addgene numbers) only match digit runs of min_digits..max_digits that are not part of a longer digit run, so dates such as 2025 or 20250205 never match.
_infer_note: If a table row has an EMPTY localization cell but its construct name contains a strong mito marker (mls, mito, cox8, tomm20/tom20), the row is treated as mito. 'mt' is excluded from this inference because it is too short.
_construct_name_note: Markers searched (as plain substrings, in this priority order) inside the plasmid NAME of mito rows to find which FP is the mito-targeted one: the FP immediately after the marker, else immediately before it (fusions like mEmeraldTOMM20, mRuby2-Mito7), else Fluorescent Protein 1. Example: pCMV_EGFP_p2a-mitoTAGRFPT -> tagRFPT (red), not EGFP.

direct_mito_keywords.rationale: Mitochondrial Localization Signal; the lab's primary tag (e.g. MAXmlsEGFP...). Matched anywhere because names glue it to other text.
Explicit mito targeting (mitoGFP, mito7, mitoTagRFPT); 'mit0' is a misspelling seen in the table (MF008).
COX8A presequence is the standard mito-targeting sequence used in the lab's constructs (MON01/05/11). cox8a is treated as direct, not as a common marker.
Outer-membrane anchor used in the lab's fusions (mEmeraldTOMM20, MON02/06).

common_markers.rationale: MitoTracker dyes stain mitochondria but are not recorded in the plasmid table.
Common abbreviation of MitoTracker Green; too short to trust without a person checking.
Common abbreviation of MitoTracker Red.
Common abbreviation of MitoTracker Deep Red (far-red channel).
MitoTracker Red CMXRos.
Membrane-potential dye that accumulates in mitochondria (red).
Membrane-potential dye that accumulates in mitochondria (red).
Ratiometric membrane-potential dye (green/red).
Classic mitochondrial membrane-potential dye.
Mitochondrial superoxide indicator dye.
Nonyl acridine orange, cardiolipin dye; short token so letter-bounded.
Green-to-red timer reporter; color depends on age, needs a person to pick the channel.
pH-sensitive mitophagy reporter; excitation-ratio imaging, not a standard 2-channel movie.
Redox sensor targeted to mitochondria; not in the lab table (plain roGFP rows are not mito).
Mito calcium sensor; not in the lab table so routed to review even though it contains 'mito'.
Common commercial mito reporter not in the lab table.
Blue mito reporter; blue channel is unusual for this pipeline.
Su9 (ATP synthase subunit 9) presequence used in mito reporters.
Outer-membrane anchor used in some mito reporters.
Outer-membrane anchor (e.g. GFP-OMP25 mito-IP tags).
Mitochondrial targeting sequence abbreviation; short token so letter-bounded.
Can mean mito-targeted (mt-GFP) but also 'mutant'; never trusted alone.
Mito transcription factor A; nucleoid marker when FP-tagged, but lab TFAM constructs (JR14, MAD001/002) are not mito-localized FPs.
Mitophagy kinase, often FP-tagged.
Mitophagy E3 ligase, cytosolic until recruited to mitochondria.
Mitofusins (outer-membrane fusion proteins), often FP-tagged.
Inner-membrane fusion protein.
Fission GTPase. Lab Drp1K38A constructs (45161, jeb026, jeb027, bkd001) carry NO mito FP, so drp1 alone must never mean MITO.
Mito transport adaptor; short token so letter-bounded.
Mito calcium uniporter; short token so letter-bounded.
Outer-membrane porin.
Matrix chaperone, matrix marker.
Cytochrome c (intermembrane space; released in apoptosis).
Mito biogenesis regulator; lab PGC1a constructs (JEB008, KRB...) are not mito-localized FPs.

fp_vocabulary.note: YFP is imaged in the green channel.
Cyan, reported in the blue bin.
Dark until photoactivated (405 nm); a mito-paGFP movie can show no mito signal outside activated regions.
Mito calcium sensor; dim at rest.

id_matching._note: A known prefix followed by a number that is NOT in the table (e.g. jeb99) is reported as unknown_id and sends the file to REVIEW unless other mito evidence exists. Single-letter prefixes (p99, p117) are too ambiguous ('p2a') to report as unknown.
